## Scratching from envelopes (patterns)

Write the scratching hand (the record position) and the crossfader into REAPER envelopes, and when the deck plays that spot it scratches exactly that way. Place the included patterns and rearrange them as automation items: copy, move, stretch and edit points.

### How it works

- The envelopes are written on two lanes of the deck's `scratch engine` track
  - **Envelope scratch**: the record position. The value is "how many beats after the grab point" (0 = the grab point, 0.5 = half a beat later). The very bottom (−0.25) means "hand off". The length of a beat is set by that deck's sample BPM
  - **Envelope fader**: the crossfader. 1 = open, 0 = closed. It is multiplied with the crossfader's own volume, and the picture fades with it
- The picture follows the crossfader opening and closing (including the envelope) directly (up to about 16 switches a second are shown). Very short switches that would end between two redraws are still shown for the next two redraws.
- The lanes' timeline positions match the time in that deck's sample (sample 1 from 0 s, sample 2 from 1 hour, and so on, in the same places as the videos). When the deck plays through a pattern's position, it grabs the record there, and when the pattern ends it lets go (with `slip` on, it returns to the normal play position after letting go)
- REAPER's own playback is not used (the video sync script reads the envelopes and passes them to the JSFX, so keep the video sync running). It works only while the deck is playing and you are not holding it with the jog or the mouse
- If you grab by hand, your hand wins. If you let go in the middle of a pattern, the pattern continues from that position

### Placing a pattern

1. Move the deck's read position to where you want the pattern (for deck A, the edit cursor position)
2. Run `reascratch_pattern.lua` and choose the deck (with two decks) and the pattern
3. It is placed as an automation item on the beat nearest the read position ("Snap" below changes this). From there you can drag it, copy it, stretch it by its edges, and add or move points like any automation item (making the lane taller makes editing easier).

- Patterns are grouped as "Basic", "Chirp", "Tear", "Flare", "Transform", "Stutter" (stutter = repeating the first 16th, 8th or 32nd; freeze and hold = stopping the sound on the spot) and more. Patterns that move the crossfader also place an item at the same position on `Envelope fader` (select both together when you move them)
- Choosing a pad (1–8) under "Put on a PATTERN pad" in the menu puts the next pattern you pick on that pad (it is only assigned, not placed; the PATTERN mode plays it)
- "Again: name" at the top of the menu places the pattern you placed last. Patterns you saved yourself are marked with "★"
- "Snap" at the bottom of the menu lets you choose where it lands: nearest beat (default), next beat (never before the head), nearest half beat, or next bar. Choosing one reopens the menu, and the choice is kept for next time. The beats are counted from the BPM and beat position where the deck is now (in a song whose tempo changes, beats far from the read position can be off)
- If you place a pattern over another, REAPER plays the two added together (to keep only one, delete or move the item underneath)
- To place the same pattern in many places, use the automation item pool (Pool); fixing one fixes them all
- **Swing**: when placing, the times of the pattern's points are shifted to the track's swing (the off-beat 16ths move later). Which value is used, typical values and the steps are in [“Fitting the swing”](#fitting-the-swing)

### Showing only the lanes you use

A deck's `scratch engine` track has about 90 parameters that can have envelopes (the ReaScratch lanes and the performance lanes, `DJ performance lanes`). REAPER's envelope list shows all of them, so `reascratch_lanes.lua` lets you show only the ones you use, by group.

1. Run `reascratch_lanes.lua` from the action list. A menu opens at the mouse cursor
2. Choose a group to show. Choose it again to hide it. A group that is shown has a check mark
   - **Hand-made scratch**: `Envelope scratch` and `Envelope fader`. Use this group to make a scratch by hand with points
   - **Recorded effects**: the video FX, filter and pad lanes written when you record a performance (laid out in the sample's time)
   - **Performance: play, sample, tempo** / **Performance: crossfader, volume, picture** / **Performance: loops, cues** / **Performance: effects**: the performance lanes (laid out on REAPER's timeline; see [“Recording and playing a performance on REAPER's timeline”](#recording-and-playing-a-performance-on-reapers-timeline))
3. The menu opens again after each choice. To finish, click outside it

- “Show only the lanes with points” shows the lanes that have points or automation items and hides the rest
- “Hide all ReaScratch lanes (points kept)” hides them all. Hidden lanes keep their points and still play
- Both decks change the same way. One run is one undo step (Ctrl+Z)

### Saving a rearranged pattern

1. On the `Envelope scratch` lane, select the item to save (the `Envelope fader` item at the same position is saved with it)
2. Run `reascratch_pattern_save.lua` and enter a name and group
3. It is saved to `Data/ReaScratch_patterns_user.lua` in the REAPER resource folder and appears in the pattern menu from then on (the same name in the same group is overwritten)

Saving removes the swing and keeps a straight version (see [“Fitting the swing”](#fitting-the-swing)).

All `.lua` files in the `Data` folder whose names start with `ReaScratch_patterns_` are loaded into the menu (the format is the same as `reascratch_patterns.lua`).

### Fitting the swing

Swing is a rhythm where, of the two 16ths in each 8th, the off-beat 16th is moved later. ReaScratch can make a deck's playback swing, and can place patterns to fit a track's swing.

**The two settings, and which one is used**

- **The deck's `Swing (16th, %)`** (setup `Beat` tab; per deck; 50–75, default 50 = straight): makes the deck's playback itself swing. Patterns placed on the deck and patterns played from the PATTERN pads use this value too
- **REAPER's grid swing** (REAPER's "Snap/Grid" settings): used only when placing patterns (no effect on the deck's playback or the PATTERN pads; see “What it does not affect” below)
- When placing a pattern, the deck's value is used if it is above 50. At 50, REAPER's grid swing is used (when swing is on, its amount is not 0 and the grid is an 8th or finer). Otherwise the pattern is placed straight
- A REAPER grid of 1/16 gives a 16th swing, 1/8 an 8th swing (the off-beat 8th moves later), and 1/32 a 32nd swing. The deck's `Swing` is for 16ths only
- There is no key or MIDI assignment. Change it in setup or in REAPER's parameter list (it can also be written as an envelope)

**Which one to use**

- **The track already swings**: leave the deck at 50 and set REAPER's grid swing to fit the track. Raising the deck's `Swing` would add more swing on top of the track's own
- **You want a straight track to swing**: raise the deck's `Swing`. Patterns you place and patterns played from the PATTERN pads get the same swing

**Typical values**

The swing value is the share of an 8th's length taken by its first 16th. A REAPER swing amount of X% corresponds to a swing of 50% + X ÷ 4.

| Swing | Deck `Swing` | REAPER swing amount | Feel |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50% | 50 | 0% | Straight |
| 54% | 54 | 16% | Very light swing |
| 58% | 58 | 32% | Light swing (measured by the author on a test track) |
| 62% | 62 | 48% | Clear swing |
| 66.7% | 67 (nearly the same) | 67% | Triplet swing (shuffle) |
| 75% | 75 | 100% | Dotted 8th + 16th |

A negative REAPER swing amount moves the off-beat 16th earlier (the deck's `Swing` cannot go below 50).

**What it affects**

- The deck's normal-speed playback (while it runs on with your hand off; also with the tempo changed, and while a reverse or half-speed pad is held): within each 8th, the first 16th is read at 0.5 ÷ swing times the speed and the second at 0.5 ÷ (1 − swing) (about 0.86x and 1.19x at 58%). Grains are used, so the pitch does not change
- The background playback of SLIP works the same way
- The picture shows the position with the swing taken out, so it moves on evenly instead of jerking every 16th
- The starts of the 8ths (beats and half beats) do not move, so beat-quantized jumps, loops and SYNC stay on the beat
- The times of the points of patterns placed with `reascratch_pattern.lua` (counted from that deck's beat grid)
- Patterns played from the PATTERN pads (when the deck's `Swing` is above 50): the times of their points are shifted as when placing. The swing is counted from the sample's beat grid (with `Q` on, from the beat the pad waited for; with `Q` off, even when it starts between beats, from the beat position where you pressed, so the 16ths change speed at the same places as the deck's playback). The `Swing` value at the start is used; changing it while the pattern plays takes effect the next time you press a pad. The picture shows the position with the swing taken out, as in normal-speed playback

**What it does not affect**

- A sample with a BPM of 0 (with no beats known, it plays straight)
- While you hold the jog or the mouse, while searching, and the spin after letting go
- REAPER's grid swing has no effect on the deck's playback or the PATTERN pads (the JSFX cannot read REAPER's grid settings). If you fit a swinging track with REAPER's grid swing and leave the deck's `Swing` at 50, the pad patterns play straight
- Patterns already placed: the swing is in the times they were placed at, so changing the value does not change them until you place them again

**Example (placing patterns on a swinging track)**

1. Set the BPM and beat position of the deck's sample ([“9. Beat-quantized jumps”](jsfx-reascratch-parameter-reference.md#9-beat-quantized-jumps-setup-beat-tab); the `T` key and `Shift`+`T`)
2. Leave the deck's `Swing` at 50. In REAPER's "Snap/Grid" settings, set the grid to 1/16, turn swing on and enter an amount (start around 32% from the table above)
3. Move the read position to where you want the pattern and place it with `reascratch_pattern.lua`
4. Play and compare with the track's 16ths by ear. If it does not fit, delete the placed item, change the amount and place it again
5. After rearranging, save it with `reascratch_pattern_save.lua` ([“Saving a rearranged pattern”](#saving-a-rearranged-pattern))

**Saving, and never swinging twice**

Saving takes out the swing in use at that moment (the deck's value or REAPER's grid swing) and keeps a straight version. Placing puts the swing in use at that moment back in, so it never swings twice. Save with the same swing you placed with (if you change the value before saving, the wrong amount is taken out and the shape is saved distorted).

### Recording a performance into envelopes

The scratching you do while REAPER is recording (record moves made by grabbing with the jog, mouse or keyboard) and the crossfader are written as automation items to the `Envelope scratch` and `Envelope fader` lanes when you stop recording. When the deck plays that section again, the scratch is reproduced as recorded.

1. Keep the video sync script running (the video sync does the writing)
2. Press REAPER's record button, play the deck and perform (to keep the sound too, prepare a track to record on; writing works even with tracks that record nothing).
3. When you stop recording, an `Envelope scratch` item is created for each stretch where your hand was on the record (named `Rec A-1`, `Rec A-2`, …; `Rec B-1`, … for deck B). If you moved the crossfader during it, an `Envelope fader` item is created at the same position too. Stretches where you only moved the crossfader without touching the record become `Envelope fader` items on their own. A stretch where the crossfader stayed closed for more than 2 beats without touching the record is taken as the deck being out of the mix, not a cut, and is not written
4. To play it back, set the crossfader to the middle and play the deck.

- Only movement while the deck is playing is written (scratching a stopped deck is not written, because envelopes only act while the deck is playing)
- The crossfader is written as "how far it closed compared with the middle position". Channel volume faders are not written.
- The items can be moved, copied and have their points edited like other patterns, and saved as patterns with `reascratch_pattern_save.lua`
- If you play the same spot twice (with slip off you passed the same place again from where you let go, you went back with a hot cue, and so on), the item written later is on top. Only performances that pass each section of the sample once are reproduced exactly as recorded (with slip on, letting go returns to the normal position, so you get exactly that).
- The video effect (this deck's type and amount, and on deck A the effect after the mix), the filter (cutoff, resonance, morph) and the TOUCH FX pads are also written to their own lanes (`Envelope vfx type`, `Envelope vfx amount`, `Envelope filter cutoff`, `Envelope filter resonance`, `Envelope filter morph`, `Envelope pad FX`, `Envelope master type`, `Envelope master amount`; one item per stretch where an effect or the filter was on). When played back, the video effect uses whichever of the recording and what you play live has the larger amount (with its type), a TOUCH FX pad is on if either has it on, and the filter recording takes effect only while the live cutoff knob is at its centre (off)
- Hot cues, loops, tempo, play/stop, sample switching and the filter type are not written (they are recorded on the lanes of the next section, [“Recording and playing a performance on REAPER's timeline”](#recording-and-playing-a-performance-on-reapers-timeline))
- If the position moves further than the lane's range (2.2 beats) while you hold the record, the excess is clipped (if you started the video sync by hand, the REAPER console shows how many points were clipped when you stop recording)
- If you use your hand over a section where an envelope (pattern) is already playing, the `Envelope scratch` items there are cut out for the length of the hand item, which replaces them (REAPER plays overlapping items added together, and when you recorded, the hand took priority over the pattern). `Envelope fader` items are not cut
- Each hand item ends with a 30 ms let-go mark (the bottom of the lane). When played back, the deck slips back there just as when you let go
- Nothing is written after recording stops
- For recordings you do not want written (such as keeping the sound of a performance made from envelope patterns), run `reascratch_record_lanes.lua` to turn it off (run it again to turn it on. The setting is saved, and if you assign it to a toolbar button, the button shows on/off)

### Recording and playing a performance on REAPER's timeline

While REAPER records, the deck operations are recorded on the "performance lanes" on REAPER's timeline. With "play the performance" on, REAPER's play button plays that performance again. It is played at the times you operated, including while a deck is stopped and inside loops (the lanes of the previous section follow the deck's sample time, so they cannot hold play / stop or loops).

What is recorded:

- Play / pause, the play position (with scratches, brakes, spinbacks, reverse and patterns), sample switching, tempo, key, PITCH PLAY
- Loops (on / off, range, roll), the CUE position, setting and clearing hot cues 1-8, adding and deleting memory cues
- The crossfader (position, the `Z` key's cut, assignment), the channel volume, mute, video opacity, the blend mode with its key threshold and softness (deck A)
- The filter (type, cutoff, resonance, Morph), the video FX type and amount (this deck's, and on deck A the master's), FX knobs 1-8 and Strobe
- Echo / bitcrusher / vibrato, the sound of the video FX, TOUCH FX (rows 1 and 2) and their amounts, the vocoder, the pattern fader
- The second APC40: the effects while CLIP STOP is held, the video FX LFO (shape, rate, depth), the picture mute, FX boost, master level and blackout

Not recorded: loading (LOAD) and what is in the slots, the setup settings, editing the BPM and the grid, the crossfader's curve, Cut-in and Fade width. SYNC is recorded but not used when playing (the recorded tempo is played).

To record:

1. Have the video sync script running
2. Press REAPER's record button, play, and stop recording
3. Far along the project (the "performance zone" from 10 hours = 36000 s on) a region `Perf 1` appears (the next recording `Perf 2` ...). On each deck's engine track, the `DJ performance lanes` lanes get one automation item per lane (`Perf A-1`, deck B `Perf B-1` ...)
   - The FX window of `DJ performance lanes` shows each lane's current value in a table (a lane without a value shows a grey “-”). The number of columns follows the window's width. The values cannot be changed in the window; edit them as envelopes ([“Showing only the lanes you use”](#showing-only-the-lanes-you-use))
   - A recording started inside the performance zone overwrites the place where it was recorded

To play it:

1. If REAPER stops playing at the end of the project, playback stops at once in the performance zone. Uncheck `Stop/repeat playback at end of project` in Options > Preferences > Audio > Playback (setup and turning "play the performance" on tell you when it is on)
2. Press `PERF PLAY` (`reascratch_perf_play.lua`) on the toolbar to turn "play the performance" on (the button lights; press again for off)
3. Put the edit cursor at the start of the region to play (`Perf 1` ...) and press REAPER's play button. Started from the middle, the decks are first set to the state at that point (loops, hot cues, effects ...)
4. When REAPER stops, the decks that played the lanes stop too

- While "play the performance" is on, the video sync does not stop REAPER's playback and does not move the edit cursor to the deck. In the performance zone the video window shows the decks (at the edit cursor while stopped). When stopped outside the zone, the cursor follows the deck as before
- An operation by hand while it plays wins until that lane's value changes again. Grabbing the jog or the record and letting go returns playback to the recorded position (as slip does)
- When REAPER stops, the `Z` key's cut, the pattern fader, the TOUCH FX pads and CLIP STOP go back to none. Other values (effect amounts ...) stay as they were at the stop
- To play one deck only, run `reascratch_perf_play_decks.lua` from the action list and choose "Deck A only" or "Deck B only" (both by default). The other deck follows only your hands
- Recording while it plays records it again (operations added by hand are included)
- While "play the performance" is on, the deck-time lanes of the previous section (`Envelope scratch` ...) are not used. Recording writes to both kinds of lanes
- The lane items are REAPER automation items, so they can be moved, copied and edited point by point

### Capturing a performance

A performance recorded in REAPER is gathered per deck as "the scratched audio" and "the video that goes with it" (raw material for audio-visual edits). It also produces a "finished mix", the sound that came out of the speakers and the picture shown in the video window, exactly as they were.

1. Run `reascratch_take.lua` to turn it on (it creates the tracks "Rec A" and "Rec B" for each deck, and "Rec Mix" for recording the finished sound. Run it again to turn it off and remove the tracks. In projects made with older versions, the tracks with Japanese names are renamed to these automatically when you run `reascratch_setup.lua` or `reascratch_take.lua`).
2. With the video sync script running, press REAPER's record button and perform
3. When you stop recording (choose to save if asked), a new project opens in another tab (the project you are performing in stays in front). It is saved in REAPER's `Data/ReaScratch_takes/`
   - "A video" track ("A 映像" when the language is Japanese): items cut and pasted from the original video, following the frames the deck showed. If you converted to all-intra on import and the original video is next to the converted one, the original (original quality) is used
   - "A audio" track ("A 音"): the deck's sound (before the crossfader and the channel volume fader)
   - "mix audio" track ("完成 音"): both decks mixed through the crossfader and the channel volume faders, then through a copy of the master's effects (limiters and so on; meters and visualizers are left out)
4. If FFmpeg is available, these videos are also made in the same folder (in the background; when done, `done` is written at the end of the `.log` file of the same name. Needs FFmpeg 5.1 or later; checked with 5.1, 6.1, 7.1 and 9.0; with 4.4 it warns you and skips video creation. To choose the FFmpeg binary to use, put its full path in REAPER's ExtState `ReaScratch` / `ffmpeg`)
   - `<name>_A.mp4` (`_B.mp4` for deck B): each deck's video with not a single frame out of place
   - `<name>_mix.mp4`: the finished mix. The crossfader (including the behaviour that keeps a switch on screen for 2 frames) and the blend (Mix, Add, Subtract, Multiply, Overlay, Soft light, Hard light) are drawn as on screen, with the "完成 音" (mix audio) attached. Luma key, Chroma key and the transitions (`Wipe right` and after) are drawn as Mix, and video effects are not drawn (the number of frames not drawn is written on the first line of the `.log`, separately for the keys, the transitions (camera moves included) and the video effects; the keys and transitions count only the frames with the crossfader between the ends)

- When REAPER renders this project, frames can be off by 1–2 (that is how REAPER's rendering behaves). When the frames must be exact, use the `.mp4` files made by ffmpeg
- The picture is aligned to when the sound was heard (the deck's sound comes about half a grain length later than the position shown in the picture, so the picture is shifted by that much)
- The per-deck videos do not contain the crossfader or video effects (they are the deck's own sound and picture)
- The finished-mix video is redrawn from the compositing values (crossfader, blend, effects) recorded by the video sync and the JSFX during recording, reproducing the video window's picture. REAPER's rendering is not used
- While recording, the video sync moves the video items to the recording position (during recording REAPER shows the picture at the recording position, not the edit cursor; they go back when you stop). REAPER draws video ahead and buffers it, so by default the crossfader and video effects appear late in the video window (about 1 s by default while playing or recording, 0.2–0.5 s even when only the decks are playing). Right-click the video window → Performance tweaks (experimental) → Video cache → **All media and video FX are not cached**. The delay drops to about 0.07 s (setup also tells you if this is not set. It takes effect immediately; no need to restart REAPER). With this setting, while a heavy video effect such as VHS is on, REAPER's screen updates slow down, and other scripts (such as visualizers) can move slowly. If that bothers you, set `Video cache` in the same menu to 0.1 s instead (a delay of about 0.1–0.2 s remains)
- While capturing, the deck tracks have at least 4 channels (8 if you are using Cue. Channels 3/4 carry the sound before the crossfader. Only channels 1/2 are sent to the master). Turning it off restores them.
